verdict.rationale: HumanLayer documents its own `humanlayer automation run` command for starting a Cloud-visible coding session from a CI job. Launch tokens support non-interactive commands, so an agent can be invoked from a pipeline. The evidence never shows this wired to build or test failures, and never shows the agent fixing a broken build or failing test, so only the triggering half of the story is evidenced. Missing for 10: documented CI-failure triggers or pipeline integrations (e.g. GitHub Actions on failed builds), examples of an agent fixing a failing build or test, how failure context is passed to the session, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can trigger an agent from CI/CD pipelines to fix a broken build or failing test

citations.quote: Use `humanlayer automation run` to run one Cloud-visible coding session from any automation environment — a CI job, a cron machine, or a script on a server.
Use a launch token for one non-interactive command.
